properties.name: ROOT CAUSE (walked, measured): nothing served answers "what changed since last time". The accepted requirement asking for it is marked satisfied by changelog_view, which reads from the last deployed release in epoch order over pinned ChangeEvents only, and the core stores no write time. So where-am-i promises an answer no read computes, and a same-day re-walk is invisible to every read tried
properties.statement:
RUN AS THE SKILL (root-cause, fetched fresh), 2026-09-28, triaging art:dev-storyflow-feedback-2026-09-27 (dev_storyflow session f56683f3, 2026-09-27 evening, its first full session on flo2.io, reflow2 0.72.0) under rule:field-feedback-issues-are-root-caused-and-ideas-are-brainstormed.

① OBSERVED, the reporter's words: "No 'what changed lately' view, and where-am-i depends on one. scan_nodes lists in id (alphabetical) order, nodes carry no created/updated date, and changelog_view is anchored to the last deployed release. To find the newest work I paged ChangeEvents and Decisions by offset. My first where-am-i summary said the latest work was 09-26 and missed a same-day re-walk; the user had to point at it." Also filed with report_manual_work, diagnosis `unknown`, because find_tools surfaced nothing. EXPECTED: some served read answers where-am-i's instruction "If nothing has changed since last time, say so plainly". NOT AFFECTED: recency for a single subject works. topic_report's `latest` and search_design's age_days/as_of read the dates that are stored.

② PRECEDENT (search_design on the raw words): the need has been ACCEPTED intent since 2026-08-07. req:what-changed-since-i-looked-and-by-whom says "The graph SHALL answer 'what changed since time T, and by whom' ... as a query" (dev_storyflow api-boss fleet ask #3). Its only SATISFIES comes from cap:changelog-view, status `verified`. On 2026-08-10, fact:the-change-ledger-records-what-moved-never-who suggested wiring changelog_view as PARTIAL coverage, "honestly labelled". It was wired as a plain SATISFIES instead. Two earlier records measured changelog_view returning nothing when events carry no AT_EPOCH pin: fact:changelog-view-is-step-two-of-the-cut-and-returns-nothing-for-a-real-cut and fact:manual-work-d1930dd9bce65676 (both 2026-09-03). fact:record-change-places-an-event-by-epoch-and-212-of-214-epochs-carry-no-date shows that an epoch places an event in a sequence, not on a calendar. The no-clock principle is deliberate: see dec:loop-status-state-not-history, and chg:the-loop-can-be-asked-what-the-record-does-not-hold ("only 2 of 2,367 nodes carry created_at ... the design has no clock, by design"). flo2's journal ask names the same "what changed while I was away" question: dec:idea-should-the-server-journal-every-write-itself and req:a-write-carries-who-made-it-and-the-server-records-that-it-happened, both proposed.

③ CANDIDATES, from the bones:
(A) INTENT/ASSURANCE. The accepted requirement was closed on paper by a capability that answers a narrower question, so the design shows nothing owed and no recency read was ever built.
(B) SUBSTRATE. With no clock in the core, several node types cannot be dated, so no general recency order can be computed.
(C) CONTRACT. The orientation skill promises an answer and names no tool for it. Its first gathering step (compare_designs against a committed export) is not offered on the hosted engine.
(D) DISCOVERABILITY. A tool exists and the agent did not find it, which is what the `unknown` diagnosis leaves open.
(E) THE OBSERVATION IS WRONG. The re-walk could have been found by a served read the agent skipped.

④ WHAT WOULD SEPARATE THEM: D and E both predict a served read that returns changes ordered by time, or that shows a same-day revision of an existing node. A, B and C predict there is none. B also predicts that date coverage on the key types is well below 100%, and C that the skill text names no tool for the promise.

⑤ RESULTS, using the 0.72.0 binary on scratch copies of reflow2's own export (5,668 nodes):
· find_tools, six phrasings ("what changed lately", "newest changes", "recent work", "what changed since last time", "list the newest changes first", "what happened while I was gone"): no tool that orders by time appears in any top 6. changelog_view appears once, at rank 6. find_skills returns where-am-i for none of them.
· Code: no served computation sorts nodes by a date. scan_nodes has no order parameter and pages by id (measured: `ce:...` ids first, then `chg:...`, alphabetically). Its brief rows carry no date. Sorting ChangeEvents by detected_at means reading all of them in full: 25 pages, about 1.06M characters. Decisions take 92 pages, about 3.4M characters, and a Decision node carries no date at all.
· Stored dates (count dated / total): ChangeEvent.detected_at 563/1158 (595 undated); TemporalFact.valid_from 614/708; Verification.last_run_at 294/349; Decision 0/829 on the node itself. 534 of 829 Decisions are dated only through authored_at or approved_at on their AUTHORED_BY edge, which scan_nodes does not return. DesignEpoch 2/287. On the hosted engine, writes_for credits each write through credit_writes, which draws AUTHORED_BY with NO date.
· changelog_view orders its window by epoch ID, not by date, and reads only the CHANGED edges of ChangeEvents pinned AT_EPOCH. From rel:v0710 it saw 9 of the 14 ChangeEvents dated since 09-26; the 4 unpinned checksum acceptances were invisible. The capability's own text says "[Unreleased] ... everything DATED after the last deployed Release", but the code uses epoch sequence, not dates.
· A scratch replay of the reporter's miss: a tiny design, exported, then a Verification re-walked (failing on 09-26, passing on 09-27) and a Decision revised. loop_status since_export listed 2 unexported ids and neither was the re-walked Verification: a revision of an existing id is invisible to an id-set baseline. changelog_view returned 0 entries.
· Hosted case: loop_status since_export on a store with no committed record reported unexported_nodes 5,668 of 5,668, with the note "EVERY node counts as new". compare_designs is absent from the hosted tool list (checked on the storyflow surface), so where-am-i's first gathering step cannot run there.
⇒ D REFUTED: there was nothing to find, so the right diagnosis was tool_missing, not unknown. E REFUTED: no served read shows the re-walk short of reading every Verification's last_run_at. A, B and C all HOLD, and they are one cause at three layers.

⑥ CLASS: an orientation skill promises an answer that no served read computes, and the requirement asking for that read is marked satisfied by an adjacent capability, so nothing in the loop says it is owed. COUNT: 2 served skill steps assume a recency read that does not exist: where-am-i ("since last time") and root-cause's Change bone ("propagate_from on recent ChangeEvents"). This is the same class as fact:root-cause-the-status-claim-was-keyed-to-nothing-and-the-catalogue-spoke-the-designs-side-not-the-askers (2026-09-14, where the agent knew 6 of 41 change events). A fix at the class would also have answered that report; rewording where-am-i alone would not.

⑦ OUT OF SCOPE; no code was changed. A test pinning the CLASS would assert three things. First, every served skill instruction that promises a change-over-time answer ("since last time", "recent", "newest") names a served tool that returns it. Second, a node written or revised after a baseline, including a REVISION of an existing id, appears in that tool's answer while an untouched node does not. Third, a Requirement whose only SATISFIES capability answers a narrower question reads as partially covered, not delivered.

REPORTER'S CONCLUSIONS. HELD: scan_nodes is id-ordered. changelog_view defaults to the last deployed release (it also takes explicit Release or Epoch ids, never a date). Nothing answers "since last time". find_tools surfaced nothing. QUALIFIED: "nodes carry no created/updated date" is true of WRITE time everywhere, but domain dates exist on about half of the ChangeEvents and on most facts and Verifications, and Decisions are dated only through their author edge, when a caller passed a date.

⑨ NOT ESTABLISHED: what storyflow's "same-day re-walk" actually was (a Verification re-run, a ChangeEvent or a finding); storyflow's design was not read. The hosted measurement is by analogy (a local store with no committed record) plus the hosted tool list, not a call on flo2. Also unknown: whether the hosted engine keeps a server-side export that since_export would use as its baseline, and storyflow's own date coverage.
